title: Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor
description:
Posted October 15, 2026

**Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor**

Doctor of Physical Therapy Program, Bert Bradford School of Health Sciences

University of Charleston

**Position Summary:**

Physical therapy core faculty (Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Professor) positions are full-time, benefit eligible, twelve-month appointments reporting directly to the Program Director of the Doctor of Physical Therapy program in the Bert Bradford School of Health Sciences. The performance of faculty will be evaluated based upon the expectations outlined in the *Faculty Manual* for faculty on the academic track. The positions are considered exempt under the Fair Labor Standards Act and classified as Fl.

The principal responsibilities of full-time faculty members at the University of Charleston are outlined in the faculty position description published as an appendix in the *Faculty Manual* and include teaching, scholarship, professional development, and service to the institution. The core faculty hold the primary responsibility for: 1) establishing and upholding program policy, 2) developing, reviewing, and revision of the curriculum, and 3) ensuring that students are professional, competent, safe and ready to progress to clinical education. Fulfillment of these responsibilities may involve weekend, evening, off-campus, and online activities as assigned. This position may be considered for remote candidates, but periodic travel to Charleston WV will be required.

Physical therapy faculty (Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Professor) primary responsibilities include teaching assigned courses, nurturing and mentoring students, maintaining an active and productive research agenda, and serving the university, community, and profession. The expected curriculum content areas or specialty practice are assigned and aligned to the respective faculty members areas of demonstrated contemporary expertise.

**Essential Responsibilities:**

A general faculty position description can be found in the *faculty manual* (appendix R). Duties specific to the physical therapy program and expectations for faculty success within the Bert Bradford School of Health Sciences include, but are not limited to:

* Fulfill all functions of a full-time faculty member as defined in the *faculty manual,* including participation in service to the University, professional development, scholarship, and innovative teaching.
* Collaborate with colleagues to develop and implement strategies aimed at enhancing student retention, engagement, and success within the Bert Bradford School of Health Sciences, including but not limited to academic advising, mentorship programs, and extracurricular activities.
* Update and maintain one’s personnel action file (PAF), including annual performance appraisals, goals, professional development plans, teaching evaluations, and peer classroom/online teaching observations.
* Develop professional self to meet expectations of contemporary teaching, service, and scholarship.
* Fulfill core faculty standards as established by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE).
* Other duties as assigned.
* **Teach (60% of total workload).**
  + Develop and deliver courses in-seat or online as assigned from either home-based or campus-based office.
  + Assess student learning and contribute to program assessment.
  + Hold regular office hours.
* **Service (20% of total workload).**
  + Actively seek opportunities to contribute expertise and leadership by serving on institutional, community, and professional committees relevant to the field of health sciences, with the goal of advancing the mission of the university and promoting professional growth within the academic community.
  + Participate in program, school, and faculty assembly meetings, graduation exercises, honors ceremonies, and Faculty Institute as requested.
  + Perform duties relating to academic advising and mentoring.
* **Scholarship (20% of total workload).**
  + Develop and implement a structured scholarship plan aimed at consistently producing high-quality blind peer-reviewed outputs including publications, platforms, posters, and/or grants.

**Qualifications:**

* Earned degree in physical therapy.
* Earned doctoral degree.
* Hold active unrestricted license as a physical therapist in an appropriate US jurisdiction and be eligible for West Virginia Physical Therapy License or Compact Privileges.
  + Out of state applicants must obtain a West Virginia license or compact privilege prior to course level teaching assignments begin.
* Developed or emerging research agenda.
* Experienced in distance education or equivalent with stable high-speed Internet connection from home office.
* Ability to travel to Charleston, WV multiple times each year potentially up to 2 weeks in duration to actively participate in onsite curricular elements.
* Demonstrated contemporary expertise to effectively manage assigned teaching load.
* Willingness to integrate Pain Neuroscience throughout the curriculum.

  

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Earned PhD or terminal academic equivalent.

* Eligible for appointment at the Assistant, Associate, or Professor rank.
* Earned Doctor of Physical Therapy clinical degree.
* Previous teaching or clinical experience working with student physical therapists or post graduate physical therapists.
* Recognized as Board Certified Specialist recognized by the American Board of Physical Therapy Specialties (ABPTS) or other advanced clinical specializations, fellowships, or certificates.
* Experienced in course and curriculum development.
* Experienced in curriculum and program assessment.
* Possess direct experience and working knowledge of the unique healthcare needs of West Virginia and greater Appalachia residents or other rural health populations.
* Previous uniformed service.
* Experienced in direct access clinical practice.
* Willingness to integrate innovative educational technologies into the curriculum including but not limited to virtual reality (VR) and artificial intelligence (AI).
* Experience as a licensed professional or as a student in case-based or problem-based curriculum delivery methodologies.
* Willingness to support and assist with clinical education activities.
* Willingness to relocate and be full-time on-the-ground at the Charleston WV campus to support on campus learning activities.

  

Interested applicants should electronically submit the documents below to:

Steven Lesh

stevenlesh@ucwv.edu

* Cover letter summarizing fit with posted qualifications

* Current CAPTE formatted CV

* Names of three professional references with contact information (email address if available)

* One-page scholarly agenda statement

* One-page instructional philosophy statement

**Applications will be accepted until the position is filled.**

**Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for current or future visa sponsorship. The University is unable to sponsor visas or green cards at this time.**

**The University of Charleston is an Equal Opportunity Employer**

**Description**

**University of Colorado Anschutz**

**School of Medicine, Department of Psychiatry**

**Job Title: Postdoctoral Fellow (1438)**

**Position #:00853946 – Requisition #:41430**

**Job Summary:**

Come join a new group forming in the Department of Psychiatry at CU Anschutz focused on applications of neuroimaging combined with brain stimulation. The projects range from basic neuroscience to cognitive neuroscience applications to clinical trials using MRI to guide personalized brain stimulation interventions. This position is a great way for neuroimaging afficionados to gain experience in the clinically relevant application of brain stimulation. Our most utilized toolbox includes fMRI guided transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), concurrent TMS/fMRI, and treatments for depression and PTSD. Prior postdocs have gone on to successful careers in industry, academia and government. No experience with brain stimulation necessary. Must be highly proficient in fMRI acquisition, processing, and analysis including a relevant publication record.

Key Responsibilities:

* fMRI processing and analysis

* Manuscript writing

* Funding application especially towards independence

* Learn neuronavigated TMS and TMS/fMRI

* Co-manage and train research coordinators, data analyst and other trainees

* Equipment set up and maintenance

* Presentation of results at scientific meetings, as appropriate

**Work Location:**

Onsite – this role is expected to work onsite and is located in Aurora, Colorado. Some initial training in Philadelphia, PA may be necessary.

**Why Join Us:**

The department of psychiatry at CU is growing rapidly. We have strong connections to the clinic and especially to interventional psychiatry. Expansion of the tools we use to other neuropsychiatric indications is already underway. There is tremendous institutional support for our neuromodulation mission that will eventually include two additional faculty co-mentors.

**Why work for the University?**

The University of Colorado offers a comprehensive benefits package. To see what benefits are available for Post-Doctoral Fellows, please visit:

* Payroll & Benefits Orientation for Post-Doctoral Fellows | University of Colorado (cu.edu)

* benefits guide cover-post-doc-2024 (cu.edu)

**Qualifications:**

**Minimum Qualifications:**

*Applicants must meet minimum qualifications at the time of hire.*

* PhD or MD/PhD in a relevant discipline such as neuroscience, psychology, bioengineering

* Extensive knowledge of fMRI acquisition, processing, analysis and interpretation

* Familiarity with relevant computing languages such as shell, bash, python, matlab, UNIX

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Outstanding publication record in high-tier scientific journals covering neuropsychiatry and neuroimaging

* Success with generating funding for research/salary coverage

* Computational and biostatistical training

* Skills in precise timing hardware control

* Some background contributing to intervention or clinical trials research

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

Candidate should have a strong background in fMRI with a publication record commensurate with their years of training. Ability to work in a dynamic multi-disciplinary environment.

**How to Apply:**

For full consideration, please submit the following document(s):

1. A letter of interest describing relevant job experiences as they relate to listed job qualifications and interest in the position

2. Curriculum vitae / Resume

3. Five professional references including name, address, phone number (mobile number if appropriate), and email address

Applications are accepted electronically ONLY at www.cu.edu/cu-careers.

Questions should be directed to: Desmond Oathes (Director), Desmond.Oathes@cuanschutz.edu .

**Screening of Applications Begins:**

Immediately and continues until position is filled. For best consideration, apply by January 15, 2027.

**Anticipated Pay Range:**

The starting salary range (*or hiring range*) for this position has been established as **HIRING RANGE:**

$63,480 - $77,076

The above salary range (*or hiring range*) represents the University’s good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation at the time of posting. This position is not eligible for overtime compensation unless it is non-exempt.

Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. The University of Colorado provides generous leave, health plans and retirement contributions that add to your bottom line.
